heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 easily processes Bambu PETG HF at high volumetric throughput up to 21 mm³/s, allowing real-world print speeds of up to 250 mm/s. As an open-frame printer with a direct-drive extruder and stainless steel nozzle, no hardware upgrades or enclosure additions are necessary.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with liquid glue or glue stick as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 21 mm³/s in the filament profile to fully leverage the high-flow characteristics of PETG HF.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' (2 mm distance) and activate 'Avoid crossing perimeters' to prevent stringing and nozzle accumulation.
Configure Pressure Advance to 0.038 s (K-factor) to maintain sharp corners and prevent seam bulging at high travel accelerations.
Set the First Layer Bed Temperature to 70°C and Subsequent Layers to 70°C, lowering part cooling fan to 0% for the first 3 layers to guarantee bed adhesion.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG HF is hygroscopic and exhibits reduced melt strength when wet, exacerbated by high melt-zone dwell time.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool at 65°C for 8 hours before printing, and increase retraction distance to 0.8 mm at 35 mm/s in OrcaSlicer.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: PEI Surface Damage or Extreme Over-Adhesion
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG has a natural affinity for PEI and can fuse chemically to the coating during cooling.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of liquid glue or PVA glue stick to act as an interfacial release barrier, and wait until the bed cools below 35°C before part removal.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Corner Warping or Lifting from Bed
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive cooling fan operation combined with room drafts on the open-frame A1 chassis.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Reduce cooling fan speed to 20% minimum / 50% maximum, set the bed temperature to 75°C, and add a 5 mm outer brim in OrcaSlicer.

faq.question: Can I print Bambu PETG HF on the Bambu Lab A1 using the stock stainless steel nozzle?
faq.answer: Yes. Bambu PETG HF contains no abrasive fibers like glass or carbon, making the stock stainless steel nozzle completely safe from accelerated wear.

faq.question: Does printing PETG HF on the A1 require an enclosure?
faq.answer: No. PETG HF does not suffer from extreme thermal shrinkage like ABS or PC, so an enclosure is unnecessary and could even cause heat creep in the extruder.

faq.question: Why is a release agent necessary on the Textured PEI Plate for PETG?
faq.answer: PETG can bond excessively to the PEI surface at 70°C, risking tearing the PEI film off the spring steel sheet upon removal; glue provides an essential sacrificial release layer.

faq.question: How do I maximize print speed without under-extruding PETG HF on the A1?
faq.answer: Maintain a nozzle temperature of 245°C–250°C to keep polymer viscosity low, and cap your maximum volumetric flow rate at 21 mm³/s in OrcaSlicer.
